**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/eu-frames-one-day-methods.html#/part-4-the-multiverse-and-the-one-path-you-declare){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 4 reads the chart that the class built, treats the idea of a multiverse at length, and closes on the analysis you preregister in your report before running it.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the multiverse tutorial, with [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd) as the companion | Your own small multiverse; where the idea comes from; the garden of forking paths; filters for inclusion; enumeration and curation; purposes of a multiverse; decomposing the variance by fork; reading a specification curve. | 20 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd) and slides | The exploratory dots from the class against the curve of 864; your bet on which decision moves estimates most, then the decomposition; where the five reanalyses and the original study are placed on the curve; what the estimator and the options that left the curve do to it. | 20 minutes |
| `try_spec()` on the [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) page | Rerun the specification you submitted, then read off your own placement among the 864 specifications of the curve and send it when the facilitator says go. | 5 minutes |
| [Reading a specification curve](../../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) and slides | What the curve leaves out; description and inference, the two jobs that a curve can do; the dependence among the 864 estimates, which means that they are not 864 tests; the permutation design and reading a curve-level test; what stands without the test. Then the discussion. | 15 minutes |
| Slides | The three critical positions, the argument that a fully specified question has one correct analysis, and what preregistration settles and what it leaves open. | 10 minutes |
| The report skeleton in the workspace, or [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) Task 5 | Complete the preregistration block before you run anything, translate it into model syntax yourself, run it, and submit with `report_result()`. Your declared result is drawn on the chart as a filled circle. | 15 minutes |
| Slides | Two points from the literature, the single analytical path, and what you take with you. | 5 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have your own placement among the 864 specifications of the curve, one specification fixed in the preregistration block of your report before it was run, and a report that contains the result of that specification, together with an answer to what the curve you joined does and does not establish.
